Commentary.Commentary: We are back. The players are out in the middle. Alick Athanaze and Justin Greaves to open for the Windies. Josh Hazlewood to bowl first. Let's go...
...THE CHASE...

Australia on the other hand, will be disappointed with the wickets they gave. A few of them just gifted it to the visitors. Some of them threw away the starts they got off to. At one time, they were 7 down for around 170 but Will Sutherland and Sean Abbott layed really well to take them out of trouble. Sean Abbott was the star with the bat and he has taken his side to a competitive total. Australia have a bowling attack which they will back to defend this. Can they do so? We will find out.

A good recovery then from the Aussies and we feel they have got a score which is around par on this slow wicket. They though were in trouble for most parts of this innings. They lost their top order quickly courtesy some excellent bowling by Alzarri Joseph and Matthew Forde! Gudakesh Motie then followed up the good work. He put up a good show with the ball too. They though will be disappointed with Oshane Thomas and Romario Shepherd! Both went for 83 runs in the 12 overs they bowled and that is too much on this wicket. Had they bowled better, Australia would have probably ended with 220. Still though, this is a score Windies will fancy but they will need to bat well.
A single to end and Australia end with 258! Outside off, this is lofted towards cover for one.

Commentary.Commentary: It is time for the second ODI between Australia and the West Indies. The first one ended how we all expected to, a comfortable win for the Aussies and we expect something similar from the hosts in the second ODI too. One thing though we have learnt after watching the Test series is that one can never write the Windies out. They won when they had to and it is the same scenario here. A win will see them stay alive in the series but a loss will see Australia clinch it with a game to. Can the rise to the occasion? We will find out.
... MATCH DAY ...

The Sydney Cricket Ground is alive with anticipation as it braces for the electrifying clash between Australia and West Indies in the 2nd ODI. The first match saw Australia dominating the proceedings, cruising to victory with 8 wickets and a substantial 11.3 overs to spare. Despite a shaky start, West Indies managed to post a respectable 231 on the board, propelled by Keacy Carty's resilient 88 and Roston Chase's gritty 59, supported by some crucial contributions from the lower order. However, they fell short of their full quota of overs, leaving room for improvement. Australia, on the other hand, recovered swiftly from the early setback of losing Travis Head cheaply. Josh Inglis and Cameron Green steadied the ship with a formidable 79-run partnership, with Inglis contributing a crucial 65 and Green a solid 77. Steven Smith then took charge, unleashing a blistering run-a-ball 79, steering Australia to a comfortable victory alongside a mammoth 149-run stand. The Aussie bowlers exhibited finesse and discipline, with Xavier Bartlett shining bright with his miserly spell, conceding a mere 19 runs while claiming a fantastic 4 wickets. Supported by Sean Abbott and Cameron Green, who both secured two scalps each, the Australian attack looked formidable. As the stage is set for the second ODI, Australia holds the upper hand in head-to-head encounters against the West Indies, especially at this historic venue where they have enjoyed significant success. With an average first innings score of 255, the pitch promises a fair contest with pacers poised to play a pivotal role. The Windies, armed with the likes of Oshane Thomas, Romario Shepherd, and Matthew Forde, are determined to bounce back with an improved and stronger bowling performance. Australia, boasting players in fine form across both batting and bowling departments, enters the contest as the probable favorite. Will the Windies rise to the occasion and level the series, breaking free from the shackles of their earlier defeat? Or will the hosts continue their dominance and clinch the series? Whose side are you on?
